dish_name: African Coconut Rice w/ Fried Chicken

sections.heading: For the coconut rice
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 min

sections.heading: For the fried chicken
items: Vegetable oil for deep frying (as needed)

method: Marinate chicken pieces in buttermilk, garlic powder, onion powder, half the paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours or overnight in the walk-in.
Rinse and soak basmati rice for 30 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
In large stock pots, heat oil, add garlic paste and bay leaves, sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add drained rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in coconut milk and water, season with salt, bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat, cover tightly, and cook 18-20 minutes until rice is fluffy.
Mix flour, cornstarch, remaining paprika, and extra salt and pepper in large trays for the dredge.
Remove chicken from buttermilk, dredge thoroughly in the seasoned flour, pressing to adhere.
Deep fry chicken in batches at 170°C for 12-15 minutes until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest fried chicken on wire racks to keep crispy.
Plate coconut rice with fried chicken, garnish with parsley and toasted coconut flakes.
notes: Contains dairy (buttermilk), gluten (flour). Coconut allergen present in rice and garnish.

dish_name: African Peanut Chicken Stew w/ Indian Bread

sections.heading: For the peanut chicken stew
items: 1.5 kg smooth peanut butter (natural, no sugar)

method: Season chicken cubes with salt, pepper, and half the paprika, then sear in batches in large pots with oil until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pots, sauté onions until golden, then add garlic paste, ginger paste, and bell peppers. Cook 3-4 minutes.
Add tomato paste and blended tomatoes, cook down for 10 minutes until the raw tomato smell disappears.
Stir in peanut butter and chicken stock, mixing until the peanut butter is fully dissolved and the sauce is smooth.
Return chicken to the pot, add remaining paprika and cayenne. Simmer covered on low heat for 35-40 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce has thickened.
For naan: combine flour, sugar, salt, and yeast. Add warm milk, yoghurt, and melted ghee. Knead into a soft dough, rest 1 hour covered.
Divide dough into 50 portions, roll into oval shapes, and cook on hot tawa or in tandoor until puffed and lightly charred.
Fold in chopped spinach into the stew in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Adjust seasoning, serve stew in bowls with warm naan on the side.
notes: Contains peanuts (major allergen), dairy (milk, yoghurt, ghee), gluten (flour). Inform customers clearly about peanut content.

sections.heading: For the aloo kheema
items: 3 kg potatoes, peeled and cubed (2 cm)

method: Heat oil in large tilting pans or stock pots. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add diced onions and cook until deep golden brown, about 12-15 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add garlic paste, ginger paste, and green chillies. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook the spices for 1 minute with a splash of water to prevent burning.
Add minced beef, breaking it up thoroughly with a paddle. Cook on high heat for 15 minutes until all moisture evaporates and mince is well browned.
Add pureed tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until oil separates from the masala.
Add cubed potatoes and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 25-30 minutes until potatoes are tender and gravy has thickened.
Finish with garam masala and fresh coriander. Adjust salt.
Serve hot with warmed Arabic bread on the side.
notes: Contains gluten (Arabic bread). Dairy-free recipe.

dish_name: Butter Chicken w/ Peas & Carrot Rice

sections.heading: For the butter chicken marinade
items: 10 kg chicken thighs (boneless, cut into chunks)

sections.heading: For the makhani gravy
items: 300 g cashew nuts, soaked and blended to paste

sections.heading: For the peas & carrot rice
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked

method: Marinate chicken in yoghurt, spices, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and salt for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Grill or roast marinated chicken at 220°C for 15-20 minutes until charred edges form. Set aside.
For gravy: heat oil and butter in large pots, sauté onions until soft, add garlic and ginger paste, cook 2 minutes.
Add tomato puree and tomato paste, cook on medium heat for 20-25 minutes until oil separates and colour deepens.
Add cashew paste, red chilli powder, sugar, and salt. Cook another 10 minutes, adding water if too thick.
Add cream and crushed kasuri methi, stir well. Add grilled chicken pieces and simmer together for 10 minutes.
For rice: heat ghee, add cumin seeds and bay leaves. Add diced carrots and peas, sauté 3 minutes.
Add soaked and drained rice, stir gently, then add water and salt. Bring to boil, cover, cook on low 18 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork, plate alongside butter chicken. Finish chicken with a swirl of cream.
notes: Contains dairy (butter, cream, yoghurt, ghee), nuts (cashews), gluten-free. Rich dish — cream and butter are essential, do not substitute.

sections.heading: For the Afghani chicken
items: 10 kg chicken leg quarters (or thighs, bone-in)

sections.heading: For the yellow rice
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked
20 g saffron strands, soaked in 200 ml warm milk

method: Blend yoghurt, cream cheese, garlic paste, ginger paste, lemon juice, white pepper, cardamom, mace, and salt into a smooth marinade.
Score chicken pieces and coat thoroughly in the marinade. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Arrange marinated chicken on oiled sheet pans, drizzle with oil, and roast at 200°C for 35-40 minutes, basting halfway, until golden and cooked through (75°C internal).
In the last 5 minutes, top chicken with grated cheese and return to oven until melted and bubbly.
For yellow rice: heat ghee in large pots, add bay leaves, cardamom, and cinnamon. Toast 1 minute.
Add drained rice and turmeric, stir to coat evenly. Pour in water and salt, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover tightly, and cook 18 minutes. Drizzle saffron milk over the top, do not stir.
Let rice rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork.
Plate yellow rice with Afghani chicken. Drizzle any pan juices over the chicken.
notes: Contains dairy (yoghurt, cream cheese, cream, ghee, cheddar). Rich and creamy — the white colour of the marinade is characteristic. Gluten-free.

sections.heading: For the chicken marinade
items: 10 kg chicken pieces (leg, thigh, on the bone)

sections.heading: For the rice
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 min

sections.heading: For the dum layering
items: 20 g saffron strands, soaked in 300 ml warm milk
1 kg flour dough for sealing (atta + water)

method: Marinate chicken with yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, spices, lemon juice, salt, fried onions, mint, and coriander. Rest for at least 3 hours.
Parboil rice in heavily salted water with whole spices until 70% cooked (rice should still have a bite). Drain immediately.
In large heavy-bottomed pots (or dum vessels), spread marinated chicken in an even layer at the bottom.
Layer parboiled rice over the chicken. Drizzle ghee and saffron milk evenly across the top.
Scatter fried onions and mint leaves over the rice layer.
Seal pots tightly with foil and then lids (or seal with atta dough). Place on high heat for 5 minutes to build steam.
Reduce to the lowest possible heat and cook (dum) for 40-45 minutes. Do not open the lid during cooking.
Break the seal, gently fold rice and chicken together from bottom up, being careful not to break the rice grains.
Serve immediately, garnished with extra fried onions and fresh coriander.
notes: Contains dairy (yoghurt, ghee, milk), gluten (atta dough for sealing — not consumed). Saffron is essential for colour and aroma. Dum technique is critical — do not skip the sealing step.

method: Season chicken with salt and pepper, then lightly dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
In large tilting pans, heat oil and butter. Sear chicken pieces until golden on both sides (do not cook through). Remove and set aside.
In the same pans, sauté onions, celery, and carrots until softened, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and mushrooms, cook 3 more minutes.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up all browned bits. Let wine reduce by half.
Add chicken stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Return chicken to the pans. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook for 30-35 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce has reduced.
For mashed potatoes: boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 25 minutes. Drain well.
Mash potatoes with butter, warm milk, cream, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until smooth. Keep warm.
Finish the fricassee by stirring in heavy cream and lemon juice. Adjust seasoning, remove bay leaves.
Serve fricassee over a bed of mashed potatoes, garnished with fresh parsley.
notes: Contains dairy (butter, cream, milk), gluten (flour for dredging). Classic French preparation — do not rush the searing step.

sections.heading: For the rice
items: 5 kg basmati or jasmine rice, cooked and cooled (ideally day-old)

sections.heading: For the stir-fry
items: 500 g green beans, cut into small pieces
500 g spring onions, sliced (white and green separated)

method: Season diced chicken with salt, white pepper, and 100 ml soy sauce. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat woks or large tilting pans over very high heat. Working in batches, sear chicken in oil until browned and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same pans, scramble eggs until just set, break into small pieces. Remove and set aside.
Add more oil, stir-fry garlic, ginger, and white parts of spring onions for 1 minute.
Add carrots, green beans, and peas. Stir-fry on high heat for 3-4 minutes until just tender.
Add cold cooked rice, breaking up any clumps. Toss vigorously over high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in remaining soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Toss to coat evenly — the rice should have a smoky colour.
Return chicken and scrambled eggs to the rice. Add sesame oil and toss everything together.
Garnish with green spring onion tops and fresh coriander. Serve immediately.
notes: Contains eggs, soy, gluten (soy sauce). Use day-old cold rice for best texture — freshly cooked rice will turn mushy.

sections.heading: For the chicken khorma
items: 10 kg chicken pieces (thigh and drumstick, on the bone)
1 kg onions, thinly sliced and fried golden (birista)
500 g raw cashews, soaked and ground to paste
300 g desiccated coconut, ground to paste
80 g khorma masala (or mild garam masala)
200 g fresh coriander and mint, chopped
20 g saffron strands, soaked in 200 ml warm milk

sections.heading: For the bagara rice
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked

method: Heat oil and ghee in large pots. Add half the fried onions and ginger-garlic paste, sauté for 3 minutes.
Add chicken pieces, turmeric, and white pepper. Sear on high heat for 5-7 minutes until chicken is lightly coloured.
Add yoghurt one ladle at a time, stirring constantly to prevent curdling. Cook until yoghurt is absorbed.
Add cashew paste, coconut paste, and enough water to create a rich gravy consistency. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in khorma masala, cardamom, mace, cream, and saffron milk. Simmer for another 10 minutes.
For bagara rice: heat oil and ghee, add cumin, mustard seeds, and fenugreek seeds. Let them splutter.
Add dried red chillies, curry leaves, and sliced onions. Fry onions until golden.
Add drained rice, turmeric, and salt. Stir gently, add water, bring to boil, then cook covered on low for 18 minutes.
Garnish khorma with remaining fried onions, fresh herbs, and a drizzle of cream. Serve alongside bagara rice.
notes: Contains dairy (yoghurt, ghee, cream), nuts (cashews), coconut. Mild and creamy — this is NOT a spicy dish. Gluten-free.

method: Combine all shawarma marinade ingredients. Coat chicken thighs thoroughly and marinate for at least 4 hours.
Roast marinated chicken on sheet pans at 220°C for 25-30 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Alternatively, grill on a flat-top in batches for more authentic charring. Slice into thin strips after resting 5 minutes.
For toum: blend garlic and salt in a food processor. Very slowly drizzle in oil while running, alternating with lemon juice and ice water, until emulsified into a thick white sauce.
Cook basmati rice with a pinch of turmeric for colour. Fluff and keep warm.
Prepare fattoush-style salad: toss tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and parsley with olive oil, lemon juice, and sumac.
Assemble bowls: base of turmeric rice, sliced shawarma chicken, dollop of hummus, pickled vegetables, and fresh salad.
Drizzle generously with toum and a final hit of olive oil.
notes: Contains sesame (hummus). Toum is dairy-free but very garlicky. Gluten-free bowl. Sumac adds essential tanginess — do not skip.

sections.heading: For Dormers' Chicken
items: 10 kg chicken thighs (boneless, cut into large chunks)

sections.heading: For the zeera (cumin) rice
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked

method: Heat oil in large pots. Add pureed onions and cook on medium-high heat for 15-20 minutes until deeply golden and oil separates.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes until raw smell disappears.
Add all ground spices (chilli, turmeric, coriander, cumin) and cook with a splash of water for 2 minutes.
Add chicken pieces and sear on high heat for 5-7 minutes. Add yoghurt and stir well.
Add tomato puree and salt. Cover and cook on medium heat for 25-30 minutes until chicken is tender and gravy is thick.
Finish with garam masala, butter, green chillies, and coarsely ground black pepper. Let rest covered 10 minutes.
For zeera rice: heat ghee in large pots, add cumin seeds and bay leaves. Toast until cumin is fragrant and darkened slightly.
Add drained rice, stir gently for 1 minute, then add water and salt. Bring to boil, cover, cook on low 18 minutes.
Fluff rice, plate alongside Dormers' Chicken, garnish with fresh coriander.
notes: Contains dairy (yoghurt, butter, ghee). Signature house dish — the generous black pepper finish is the hallmark. Gluten-free.

dish_name: Dormers' Kabab w/ Chutney & Arabic Bread

sections.heading: For the kababs
items: 10 kg minced beef or lamb (20% fat content)

method: Combine minced meat with onions, ginger-garlic paste, green chillies, herbs, all spices, salt, eggs, and breadcrumbs. Mix thoroughly until the mixture holds together.
Cover and refrigerate the mixture for at least 1 hour to firm up and allow flavours to meld.
Shape into oval kababs (about 120-150g each), keeping hands lightly oiled to prevent sticking.
Cook kababs on a well-oiled flat-top griddle or in shallow oil in tilting pans, turning once, until deeply browned and cooked through (about 4-5 minutes per side).
For green chutney: blend all chutney ingredients in food processors until smooth. Adjust salt and chilli to taste.
Warm Arabic bread on the griddle or in a low oven.
Serve 2-3 kababs per portion with a generous side of green chutney, warm Arabic bread, onion rings, and lemon wedges.
notes: Contains eggs, gluten (breadcrumbs, Arabic bread). Kabab mixture must be cold when shaping — warm mince will not hold shape.

sections.heading: For the hot sauce
items: 500 ml sriracha or red chilli sauce

sections.heading: For bowl assembly
items: 5 kg basmati rice, cooked with turmeric

method: Marinate chicken thighs in lemon juice, oil, and all spices for at least 4 hours.
Cook chicken on a flat-top griddle at high heat until well-charred, about 6-7 minutes per side. Rest briefly, then chop into small pieces on the griddle (Halal Guys style).
For white sauce: whisk together mayonnaise, yoghurt, vinegar, sugar, garlic powder, pepper, and salt. Thin with water to a drizzle-able consistency. Chill until service.
For hot sauce: blend sriracha with chilli flakes, vinegar, garlic powder, and salt.
Cook basmati rice with turmeric, a knob of butter, and salt. Keep warm.
Assemble bowls: bed of turmeric rice, chopped griddled chicken, shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes.
Drizzle generously with white sauce and a stripe of hot sauce. Add pickled jalapeños on the side.
Serve immediately while chicken is hot and vegetables are crisp.
notes: Contains dairy (yoghurt, mayonnaise contains eggs). White sauce is the signature — must be tangy and garlicky. Gluten-free bowl.

sections.heading: For the lamb pilaf
items: 6 kg lamb shoulder (bone-in, cut into chunks)
5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked

sections.heading: For the salad
items: 500 g red onion, thinly sliced into rings

method: Heat oil in large heavy pots. Sear lamb pieces in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, fry sliced onions until dark golden. Add julienned carrots and cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Return lamb to the pot, add cumin, peppercorns, bay leaves, and whole garlic heads. Pour in water/stock and bring to a boil.
Simmer covered for 45 minutes until lamb is nearly tender. Add soaked chickpeas and raisins, cook another 15 minutes.
Taste the broth and adjust salt — it should be slightly over-seasoned as the rice will absorb it.
Spread drained soaked rice evenly over the lamb and broth. Do not stir. The liquid should sit about 2 cm above the rice. Add more hot water if needed.
Bring to a boil uncovered, then reduce heat to lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook for 25 minutes until rice is done.
For the salad: toss tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and radishes with lemon juice, olive oil, dill, salt, and sumac.
To serve, invert the pilaf onto large platters so lamb sits on top of the rice. Serve salad on the side.
notes: Dairy-free, gluten-free. Central Asian style pilaf — the layering technique (rice over meat, no stirring) is critical for proper texture.

sections.heading: For the lamb stroganoff
items: 8 kg lamb leg (boneless, cut into thin strips)

sections.heading: For the riz pilaf
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked
500 g vermicelli (sha'riyya), broken into small pieces

method: Season lamb strips with salt, pepper, and half the paprika. Dredge lightly in flour.
In large pans, heat oil over very high heat. Sear lamb strips in small batches (do not crowd) until browned. Set aside.
Reduce heat, add butter, and sauté onions until caramelised (15 minutes). Add mushrooms and garlic, cook 5 more minutes.
Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Deglaze with Worcestershire sauce and stock.
Add remaining paprika, smoked paprika, and Dijon mustard. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until sauce thickens.
Return lamb to the sauce. Remove from heat and fold in sour cream. Do not boil after adding sour cream or it will curdle.
For riz pilaf: melt butter in large pots, toast broken vermicelli until deep golden brown, stirring constantly.
Add rice, bay leaves, and cinnamon. Stir 1 minute, then add stock and salt. Boil, cover, cook on low 18 minutes.
Fluff pilaf with a fork. Serve stroganoff over riz pilaf, garnished with fresh parsley.
notes: Contains dairy (butter, sour cream), gluten (flour, vermicelli, Worcestershire sauce). Do not boil after adding sour cream.

sections.heading: For the malai tikka marinade
items: 10 kg chicken breast (boneless, cut into tikka-size cubes)
100 g green chillies, ground to paste

sections.heading: For the lemon rice
items: 5 kg basmati rice, cooked and cooled slightly

method: Combine cream cheese, yoghurt, cream, garlic paste, ginger paste, green chilli paste, lemon juice, all dry spices, cornflour, and mustard oil into a smooth marinade.
Coat chicken cubes thoroughly in the marinade. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Thread marinated chicken onto skewers or spread on oiled sheet pans. Roast at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until lightly charred with creamy white-green colour.
Alternatively, cook in tandoor for more authentic smoky char.
For lemon rice: heat oil in large pans, add mustard seeds and let them pop. Add urad dal and peanuts, fry until golden.
Add curry leaves, green chillies, and ginger. Sauté 1 minute.
Add turmeric and salt, then fold in the cooked rice gently, tossing to coat evenly.
Remove from heat, add fresh lemon juice, and toss. The rice should be bright yellow with a tangy aroma.
Plate lemon rice with malai tikka pieces on top. Serve with green chutney on the side.
notes: Contains dairy (cream cheese, yoghurt, cream), nuts (peanuts in rice). Malai tikka should be creamy white — not red like tandoori. Gluten-free.

dish_name: Meatballs w/ Mashed Potatoes & Mushroom Sauce
method: Soak breadcrumbs in milk until softened. Combine with minced beef, onions, garlic, eggs, parsley, Parmesan, and all seasonings. Mix until just combined — do not overwork.
Portion meatballs into 60-70g balls (about 3 per serving). Place on oiled sheet pans.
Sear meatballs in batches in hot oil on a flat-top or in pans until browned on all sides. Transfer to deep hotel pans.
Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
For mushroom sauce: melt butter in large pots, sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and it evaporates.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms, stir to coat, and cook the roux for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in beef stock, then Worcestershire sauce. Simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes. Finish with cream and thyme.
Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender. Drain well, mash with butter, warm milk, cream, salt, and pepper.
Serve meatballs over mashed potatoes, ladled generously with mushroom sauce.
notes: Contains dairy (butter, cream, milk, Parmesan), eggs, gluten (breadcrumbs, flour). Do not overwork the meatball mixture — it makes them tough.

sections.heading: For the beef
items: 8 kg beef chuck or shoulder, cut into strips

sections.heading: For the cilantro-lime rice
items: 5 kg basmati or long-grain rice, cooked

sections.heading: For the black beans
items: 3 kg black beans (canned, drained and rinsed)

sections.heading: For bowl toppings
items: 2 kg pico de gallo (tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime)

method: Marinate beef strips in lime juice, oil, and all spices for at least 2 hours.
Cook beef on a very hot flat-top griddle or in large pans, searing until caramelised and cooked through. Chop into smaller pieces on the griddle. Keep warm.
For black beans: sauté onions and garlic in oil, add cumin, then add beans. Cook for 10 minutes with a splash of water, mashing slightly for a creamy texture.
Cook rice, then fold in lime juice, chopped cilantro, oil, and salt while still warm. Toss to distribute evenly.
For pico de gallo: dice tomatoes, onion, and jalapeño. Toss with cilantro, lime juice, and salt.
Prepare guacamole: mash avocados with lime juice, diced onion, cilantro, salt, and a pinch of cumin.
Assemble bowls: cilantro-lime rice base, seasoned black beans, griddled beef, pico de gallo, corn, dollop of sour cream and guacamole.
Top with shredded lettuce, pickled jalapeños, and fresh cilantro.
notes: Contains dairy (sour cream). Gluten-free. Guacamole must be made close to service time to prevent browning — press cling film directly on surface if made early.

sections.heading: For the chicken tagine
items: 20 g saffron strands, soaked in 300 ml warm water
500 g preserved lemons, chopped (or 200 ml lemon juice + zest of 20 lemons)

sections.heading: For the couscous
items: 4 litres boiling water or chicken stock

method: Season chicken with salt, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, and paprika. Let sit for 30 minutes.
Heat olive oil in large heavy pots or braising pans. Sear chicken pieces skin-side down until deeply golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté onions until soft and golden. Add garlic and ginger, cook 2 minutes.
Add saffron water, preserved lemons, honey, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot, cover, and braise on low heat for 45 minutes until chicken is fall-off-the-bone tender.
Add olives in the last 10 minutes of cooking. Adjust seasoning.
For couscous: place couscous in large hotel pans, add salt and cinnamon. Pour over boiling stock, cover tightly with foil, and let steam for 10 minutes.
Fluff couscous with a fork, fold in butter, diced apricots, and most of the toasted almonds.
Serve tagine over couscous, garnished with fresh coriander and remaining almond flakes.
notes: Contains dairy (butter), gluten (couscous is wheat-based), nuts (almonds). Preserved lemons are essential for authentic flavour — do not substitute with fresh alone.

sections.heading: For the peri-peri chicken
items: 10 kg chicken leg quarters (or whole legs, split)
500 g red bird's eye chillies (or peri-peri chillies)

sections.heading: For the jolof rice
items: 5 kg long-grain or basmati rice, washed
5-10 scotch bonnet peppers (whole, for heat without breaking)

method: Blend all peri-peri marinade ingredients (chillies, bell peppers, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, oil, spices, sugar) into a smooth sauce.
Score chicken pieces and coat heavily in peri-peri sauce. Marinate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Grill or roast chicken at 200°C for 35-40 minutes, basting with reserved peri-peri sauce every 10 minutes, until charred and cooked through (75°C internal).
For jolof rice: heat oil in very large pots. Fry blended onions until all the moisture evaporates and it starts to brown.
Add tomato paste and fry for 5 minutes until it darkens. Add blended tomatoes and bell peppers. Cook on high for 20-25 minutes until the oil floats on top (the tomato frying stage is essential).
Add garlic paste, ginger paste, thyme, curry powder, and bay leaves. Cook 2 more minutes.
Add washed rice and stir to coat in the tomato base. Pour in chicken stock, add salt and whole scotch bonnets on top (do not pierce them).
Cover tightly with foil and lid. Cook on low heat for 30-35 minutes. Do not open or stir until done.
Remove scotch bonnets, fluff rice gently. Serve jolof rice with peri-peri grilled chicken.
notes: Dairy-free, gluten-free. Very spicy — adjust bird's eye chilli quantity based on batch tasting. Scotch bonnets in jolof are for aroma, not to be burst. Tomato frying stage for jolof cannot be rushed.

sections.heading: For the marinara enhancement
items: 100 ml extra virgin olive oil (for finishing)

method: Heat olive oil in large stock pots. Cook the soffritto (onions, carrots, celery) over medium heat for 12-15 minutes until soft and starting to caramelise.
Add garlic, cook 2 minutes. Push vegetables to the sides and add minced beef in batches, breaking up well. Brown the meat thoroughly, letting moisture evaporate.
Add tomato paste and cook for 3-4 minutes until it darkens. Deglaze with red wine and let it reduce.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, dried herbs, bay leaves, sugar, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cook uncovered for at least 1.5-2 hours, stirring occasionally, until rich and thick.
In the last 30 minutes, taste and adjust seasoning. Remove bay leaves.
Cook spaghetti in heavily salted boiling water until al dente (1 minute less than package directions). Reserve 2 litres of pasta water before draining.
Toss drained spaghetti with a portion of the Bolognese sauce and a splash of pasta water to create a glossy coating.
Plate spaghetti with additional sauce on top, finish with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.
notes: Contains gluten (spaghetti), dairy (Parmesan). Long slow cook is essential — do not rush the sauce. Pasta water is key to the final sauce consistency.

dish_name: Thai Chicken Curry w/ Coconut Rice

sections.heading: For the Thai green/red curry
items: 1 kg Thai curry paste (green or red, store-bought or house-made)
500 g Thai eggplant or regular eggplant, cubed
100 g fresh red chillies, sliced (for garnish)

method: Heat oil in large woks or tilting pans. Add curry paste and fry for 3-4 minutes until fragrant and the oil splits from the paste.
Add 1 litre of coconut cream and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring continuously, until the cream reduces and becomes oily (this is called 'cracking' the coconut cream).
Add chicken pieces and sear in the curry paste mixture for 5-7 minutes until well coated and starting to cook.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a simmer. Add eggplant and bamboo shoots. Cook for 15-20 minutes until chicken is done and vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar — the balance should be savoury-sweet-spicy. Add kaffir lime leaves and bell peppers in the last 5 minutes.
For coconut rice: combine washed jasmine rice, coconut milk, water, salt, sugar, and pandan leaves in large rice cookers or pots.
Bring to a boil, reduce to low, cover and cook for 18-20 minutes. Remove pandan leaves.
Fold in Thai basil leaves into the curry just before serving — they wilt quickly and should stay vibrant.
Serve curry in bowls over coconut rice, garnished with sliced red chillies and extra Thai basil.
notes: Contains coconut, fish sauce (fish allergen). Dairy-free, gluten-free. Cracking the coconut cream is a critical step for authentic flavour — do not skip.

sections.heading: For the vegetable biryani
items: 5 kg basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 min
500 g green beans, cut into 2 cm pieces
1 kg onions, thinly sliced and fried (birista)

sections.heading: For the dum layering
items: 20 g saffron strands, soaked in 200 ml warm milk

method: Heat oil in large pots, sauté ginger-garlic paste for 2 minutes. Add all vegetables (except peas) and cook for 5-7 minutes.
Add yoghurt, chilli powder, turmeric, biryani masala, and salt. Cook the vegetable masala for 10 minutes until vegetables are half-cooked.
Add peas, half the mint and coriander, and half the fried onions. Remove from heat.
Parboil rice in salted water with whole spices until 70% cooked. Drain.
Layer rice over vegetable masala in large dum vessels. Drizzle ghee and saffron milk. Top with remaining fried onions and mint.
Seal with atta dough or foil + lid. Cook on high 5 minutes, then lowest heat for 35-40 minutes.
For Dormers' Chicken: heat oil, cook onion puree until deep golden (15-20 min). Add ginger-garlic paste, ground spices, then chicken.
Add tomato puree and salt, cover and cook 25-30 minutes. Finish with garam masala, coarse black pepper, butter, and coriander.
Serve veg biryani on plates with Dormers' Chicken alongside. Garnish biryani with fried onions and fresh herbs.
notes: Contains dairy (yoghurt, ghee, butter, milk for saffron, paneer if used), gluten (atta dough seal — not consumed). Two-component dish: the biryani is vegetarian, the chicken is served as a separate side.

method: Roast whole eggplants directly over open flame or in a hot tandoor until the skin is fully charred and the flesh is completely soft and smoky. Allow to cool, then peel off the charred skin and mash the flesh roughly.
Heat mustard oil in large heavy-bottomed pans until smoking point, then let it cool slightly. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until deep golden brown, about 12–15 minutes on high flame.
Add minced ginger, garlic, and green chillies. Cook for 3–4 minutes until raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook until tomatoes break down and oil separates, about 10 minutes.
Add the mashed roasted eggplant and mix well. Cook on medium heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring frequently to develop flavour and prevent sticking.
Season with garam masala and salt. Fold in fresh coriander leaves.

For the roti: knead whole wheat flour with salt and water into a smooth, pliable dough. Rest for 20 minutes. Divide into 100 g portions, roll into rounds, and cook on a hot tawa with light oil until golden spots appear on both sides.
Portion the bharta into service containers and serve hot alongside roti.
notes: Contains gluten (wheat roti). Mustard oil is a potential allergen.

dish_name: Butter Paneer w/ Carrot & Peas Rice

sections.heading: For the butter paneer gravy
items: 5 kg paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes
300 g cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste

sections.heading: For the carrot and peas rice

method: Soak basmati rice in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Lightly fry paneer cubes in hot oil until golden on the edges. Drain on paper and reserve.
In large heavy pans, melt butter and sauté onion puree until light golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 3 minutes.
Add tomato puree and cook on medium heat for 25–30 minutes until the gravy darkens and oil separates from the masala.
Stir in cashew paste, kashmiri chilli powder, sugar, and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, adding water to reach a smooth, creamy consistency.
Finish the gravy with cream, crushed kasuri methi, and garam masala. Fold in fried paneer cubes gently. Keep warm.
For the rice: heat ghee in large pots, add cumin seeds, bay leaves, and cardamom. Sauté diced carrots for 3 minutes, then add peas and rice. Stir gently.
Add measured water and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on low heat for 18–20 minutes until rice is fluffy and grains are separate.
Fluff rice with a fork, removing whole spices from the top. Serve butter paneer alongside carrot and peas rice.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer, butter, cream, ghee) and tree nuts (cashews).

sections.heading: For the dal nawabi
items: 200 g cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste

method: Wash chana dal thoroughly and soak for 1 hour. Pressure cook with turmeric and salt until soft but not mushy — each grain should hold its shape slightly.
Heat ghee in large pans, add cumin seeds, and let them crackle. Add sliced onions and fry until deep golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes. Add tomato puree, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook until oil separates, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the cooked chana dal and cashew paste. Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Adjust consistency with water — it should be rich and thick, not watery.
Finish with cream, crushed kasuri methi, garam masala, and fresh coriander. Adjust salt.
For the zeera rice: soak basmati rice for 30 minutes and drain. Heat ghee in large pots, add cumin seeds and bay leaves, let them splutter.
Add drained rice and stir gently for 2 minutes. Add water and salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low heat for 18 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Serve dal nawabi in bowls alongside zeera rice.
notes: Contains dairy (ghee, cream) and tree nuts (cashews).

sections.heading: For the Dormers' paneer
items: 5 kg paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes
200 g cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste

method: Shallow-fry paneer cubes in batches until light golden. Drain and set aside.
Heat ghee in large heavy-bottomed pans. Add onion puree and cook on medium heat until rich golden brown, stirring frequently — about 15 minutes.

Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes. Add tomato puree, kashmiri chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook until masala is well-fried and oil separates, about 20 minutes.
Stir in cashew paste and whisked yoghurt. Cook for 5 minutes on low heat, stirring constantly to prevent curdling.
Add water as needed for a velvety, medium-thick gravy. Simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in sugar and salt.
Finish with cream, crushed kasuri methi, and garam masala. Fold in fried paneer cubes and let them absorb the flavours for 5 minutes on low heat.
For the zeera rice: soak basmati rice 30 minutes, drain. Heat ghee, crackle cumin seeds and bay leaves. Add rice, stir 2 minutes, add water and salt. Boil, cover, cook low for 18 minutes.
Garnish paneer with fresh coriander. Serve alongside fluffy zeera rice.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer, ghee, cream, yoghurt) and tree nuts (cashews).

dish_name: Dum Aloo & Dal w/ Arabic Bread

sections.heading: For the dal
items: Whole dried red chillies for tadka

method: Prick baby potatoes all over with a fork. Deep fry in batches until golden brown and slightly crispy on the outside. Drain and set aside.
Heat oil in large pans, add cumin seeds. Add onion puree and cook until deep golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes.
Add tomato puree, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, coriander powder, and fennel powder. Cook until oil separates, about 15 minutes.

Lower heat, add whisked yoghurt gradually, stirring continuously. Add fried potatoes and enough water to create a thick gravy. Cover and simmer (dum) on low heat for 25–30 minutes until potatoes are tender and flavours have penetrated.
Finish dum aloo with garam masala and adjust salt.
For the dal: wash and pressure cook moong dal with turmeric and salt until completely soft and smooth. Whisk to an even consistency.

Prepare tadka: heat ghee, add cumin seeds, dried red chillies, chopped onions, and ginger-garlic paste. Fry until golden. Add chopped tomatoes and red chilli powder. Cook 5 minutes, then pour into the cooked dal. Simmer together for 10 minutes.
Warm Arabic bread in batches in an oven at 180°C for 2–3 minutes before service.
Serve dum aloo and dal side by side with warm Arabic bread.
notes: Contains dairy (yoghurt, ghee) and gluten (Arabic bread).

sections.heading: For the jolof rice
items: 300 g scotch bonnet or habanero peppers, blended (adjust to taste)

sections.heading: For the grilled veggies
items: 500 g red onions, cut into thick rings
Salt and black pepper to taste

method: Wash parboiled rice in several changes of water and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.
Blend tomatoes, red bell peppers, and scotch bonnet peppers into a smooth puree. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in very large heavy pots. Fry chopped onions until softened. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Fry for 5 minutes until the paste darkens.
Pour in the blended pepper-tomato mixture. Cook on high heat for 30–40 minutes, stirring regularly, until the mixture reduces significantly and oil floats on top — this is the base of good jolof.
Add thyme, curry powder, white pepper, bay leaves, and salt. Stir in the vegetable stock and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the drained rice, stir once, then reduce heat to the lowest setting. Cover the pot tightly with foil and then the lid to trap all steam. Cook for 30–35 minutes without opening.

For the grilled veggies: toss zucchini, bell peppers, eggplant, and red onions with olive oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Grill on hot flat-tops or sheet pans in a 220°C oven for 15–20 minutes until charred and tender.
Fluff jolof rice with a fork. The bottom layer should have a slight crust (the prized 'socarrat'). Serve rice topped with grilled vegetables.

sections.heading: For the kadhai paneer
items: 5 kg paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 kg bell peppers (mixed), cut into chunks
50 g dried red chillies, coarsely crushed

method: Dry roast crushed coriander seeds and dried red chillies in a kadhai or dry pan until fragrant. This is the kadhai masala — the signature flavour. Set aside.
Heat oil in large kadhais or heavy pans. Sauté onions until softened, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and half the julienned ginger, cook 2 minutes.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, and kashmiri chilli powder. Cook on high heat until the masala is thick and oil separates, about 15 minutes.
Add paneer cubes and bell pepper chunks. Toss everything together and cook for 5–7 minutes on high heat — the veggies should retain a slight crunch.
Sprinkle in the prepared kadhai masala, garam masala, and crushed kasuri methi. Toss well. Adjust salt.
Garnish with remaining julienned ginger and fresh coriander.
For the rice: wash basmati rice and soak 30 minutes. Bring salted water to a rolling boil, add rice, cook uncovered until just done (about 10 minutes). Drain, cover, and let steam for 5 minutes.
Serve kadhai paneer hot alongside steamed basmati rice.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer).

sections.heading: For the tangy beans
items: 3 kg red kidney beans (rajma), soaked overnight, or canned equivalent
Salt and black pepper to taste

method: Boil peeled and quartered potatoes in large pots of salted water until fork-tender, about 25–30 minutes. Drain thoroughly.

Mash potatoes using a ricer or masher (avoid food processor — it makes them gluey). Add warm butter, warm milk, cream, garlic powder, salt, and white pepper. Mix until smooth and creamy. Keep warm in covered pans.
If using dried kidney beans: boil soaked beans in fresh water until completely tender, about 1–1.5 hours. Drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in large pans. Sauté diced onions until softened, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 10 minutes until tomatoes break down. Add smoked paprika, cumin, and mustard powder. Stir well.
Add cooked beans, apple cider vinegar, and brown sugar. Mix thoroughly. Add enough water to create a saucy consistency. Simmer for 20 minutes on low heat.
Season tangy beans with salt and pepper. Finish with fresh parsley.
Serve a generous scoop of mashed potatoes topped with tangy beans.
notes: Contains dairy (butter, milk, cream).

dish_name: Methi Matar Paneer w/ Arabic Bread

sections.heading: For the methi matar paneer
items: 4 kg paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes
500 g fresh fenugreek leaves (methi), washed and chopped
150 g cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste

method: Wash fresh fenugreek leaves thoroughly in several changes of water to remove grit. Chop finely. Blanch in boiling water for 1 minute and drain to remove bitterness.
Lightly fry paneer cubes until golden edges. Drain and set aside.
Heat ghee in large pans, add cumin seeds. Add onion puree and cook until golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes. Add tomato puree, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, and coriander powder. Cook until oil separates, about 15 minutes.
Stir in cashew paste and cook for 5 minutes. Add water to achieve a medium-thick gravy. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add green peas and blanched methi leaves. Cook for 8–10 minutes until peas are tender.
Fold in fried paneer cubes. Finish with cream and garam masala. Adjust salt.
Warm Arabic bread in the oven at 180°C for 2–3 minutes before service.
Serve methi matar paneer with warm Arabic bread.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer, ghee, cream), tree nuts (cashews), and gluten (Arabic bread).

sections.heading: For the paneer Afghani
items: 5 kg paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes
500 g cream cheese or hung curd, whisked smooth
200 g cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste

method: Marinate paneer cubes with half the cream cheese, cornflour, cardamom powder, white pepper, and salt. Let sit for 20 minutes.
Shallow-fry marinated paneer cubes in batches until light golden on all sides. Drain on paper towels.
In large pans, melt butter. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies. Sauté on low heat for 3 minutes — do not brown.
Add the remaining cream cheese, cashew paste, and heavy cream. Stir on low heat until the sauce is smooth and creamy, about 10 minutes.
Add mace powder and adjust salt and white pepper. The gravy should be white/cream-coloured and rich.
Fold in fried paneer cubes and grated cheddar. Stir gently until cheese melts into the sauce. Keep warm.

For the yellow rice: soak basmati rice 30 minutes. Heat ghee, add cumin seeds, bay leaves, and cardamom. Add drained rice and turmeric, stir gently. Add water and salt, boil, then cover and cook on low for 18 minutes.
Garnish Afghani paneer with coriander. Serve alongside fragrant yellow turmeric rice.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer, cream cheese, cream, butter, cheddar, ghee) and tree nuts (cashews).

sections.heading: For the paneer lababdar
items: 5 kg paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes
200 g cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste

method: Fry paneer cubes until light golden. Drain and reserve.
Melt butter in large pans. Add onion puree and cook until golden, about 12 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes.
Add tomato puree, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, and coriander powder. Cook until masala thickens and oil separates, about 20 minutes.
Stir in cashew paste and sugar. Add water for a smooth, flowing gravy. Simmer 10 minutes.
Finish with cream, crushed kasuri methi, and garam masala. Fold in paneer cubes. Keep warm.
For the lemon rice: cook basmati rice in salted boiling water until just done, drain, and spread on trays to cool slightly.
Heat ghee in wide pans. Add mustard seeds and let them pop. Add urad dal and fry until golden. Add curry leaves, green chillies, and peanuts. Toss for 1 minute.
Add turmeric and the cooked rice. Drizzle lemon juice evenly over the rice. Toss gently with a fork until uniformly yellow and well seasoned. Adjust salt.
Serve paneer lababdar alongside tangy lemon rice.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer, butter, cream, ghee), tree nuts (cashews), and peanuts.

sections.heading: For the paneer tikka marinade
items: 5 kg paneer, cut into 3 cm cubes

sections.heading: For the tikka vegetables
items: 1 kg bell peppers (mixed), cut into 3 cm squares
1 kg onions, cut into 3 cm squares and layers separated

method: Whisk together yoghurt, mustard oil, ginger-garlic paste, all dry spices, lemon juice, and salt to make the tikka marinade.
Add paneer cubes and vegetable pieces (bell peppers, onions, tomatoes) to the marinade. Mix gently to coat evenly. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, up to 4 hours.
Thread marinated paneer and vegetables onto skewers, alternating pieces for even cooking.
Cook in a preheated tandoor or very hot oven (250°C) for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until edges are charred and smoky. Alternatively, use a flat-top grill brushed with oil.
Baste with a little melted butter during the last 2 minutes of cooking for extra richness.
Remove from skewers, sprinkle generously with chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.
Warm Arabic bread in the oven at 180°C for 2–3 minutes.
Serve paneer tikka on warm Arabic bread with green chutney on the side.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer, yoghurt). Contains gluten (Arabic bread). Mustard oil is a potential allergen.

method: Boil cauliflower, carrots, and peas together until very soft. Drain and mash roughly — the texture should be chunky, not pureed.
Heat generous butter in very large flat pans (tawa-style if possible). Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down completely, about 10 minutes.
Add all mashed vegetables (potatoes, cauliflower-carrot-peas mix) and diced bell peppers. Mix well.

Add pav bhaji masala, kashmiri chilli powder, turmeric, and salt. Mash everything together on the tawa using a potato masher, pressing and mixing vigorously. Add water as needed to get a thick, scoopable consistency.
Cook on medium heat for 20–25 minutes, continuously pressing and mixing. Add extra butter — pav bhaji should be generously buttery.
To serve: split pav buns, butter both cut sides generously, and toast on a hot tawa until golden and crispy.
Serve bhaji topped with a knob of butter, chopped coriander, and a squeeze of lemon alongside hot toasted pav.
notes: Contains dairy (butter) and gluten (pav buns).

sections.heading: Ingredients
items: 3 kg canned San Marzano or Italian plum tomatoes, crushed by hand
Salt and black pepper to taste

method: Bring very large pots of heavily salted water to a rolling boil (the water should taste like the sea). Cook penne until al dente — about 1 minute less than package instructions. Reserve 2 litres of starchy pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in large wide pans. Add sliced garlic and chilli flakes, cook on low heat for 2 minutes until garlic is fragrant but not browned.
Add diced onions and sauté until completely softened and translucent, about 10 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, sugar, and salt. Simmer on medium heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and the raw tomato flavour is gone.
Tear most of the basil leaves and stir into the sauce in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Add drained penne to the sauce. Toss vigorously over heat for 2–3 minutes, adding reserved pasta water a ladle at a time to achieve a glossy, clinging sauce.
Serve in portions, topped with grated Parmesan and a few fresh basil leaves.
notes: Contains gluten (wheat pasta) and dairy (Parmesan cheese).

dish_name: Plantballs w/ Mashed Potatoes & Mushroom Sauce

sections.heading: For the plantballs
items: 3 kg plant-based mince (soya or pea protein based)

sections.heading: For the mashed potatoes
items: Salt and white pepper to taste

method: Mix plant-based mince with breadcrumbs, finely diced onions, garlic, soy sauce, smoked paprika, onion powder, black pepper, and salt. Shape into 40 g balls — you should get roughly 100 plantballs.
Bake plantballs on oiled sheet pans at 200°C for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until firm and browned. Alternatively, pan-fry in batches in vegetable oil.
For mashed potatoes: boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender. Drain and mash. Beat in warm butter, warm milk, cream, salt, and white pepper until smooth and fluffy. Keep warm.

For mushroom sauce: melt butter in large pans. Add onions and garlic, sauté until soft. Add sliced mushrooms and cook on high heat until they release all moisture and begin to brown, about 15 minutes.
Reduce heat, sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and stir for 3 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste.
Gradually add warm milk while stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Add thyme, pepper, and salt. Simmer until sauce thickens to a rich, velvety consistency, about 10 minutes. Finish with cream.
Plate with a generous scoop of mashed potatoes, 2 plantballs per portion, and ladle mushroom sauce over the top.
notes: Contains gluten (breadcrumbs, flour), dairy (butter, milk, cream), and soy (soy sauce, possibly plant mince).

sections.heading: For the rajma aloo
items: 3 kg red kidney beans (rajma), soaked overnight
2 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into large cubes

method: Drain soaked rajma, rinse, and pressure cook in fresh water with a pinch of salt until completely tender — about 25–30 minutes after full pressure. Beans should be soft enough to mash between fingers. Reserve the cooking liquid.
Boil potato cubes separately until just tender but still holding shape. Drain.
Heat oil in large pots, add cumin seeds. Add chopped onions and cook until golden brown, about 12 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 3 minutes. Add tomato puree, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, and coriander powder. Cook until oil separates, about 15 minutes.

Add cooked rajma with their cooking liquid and boiled potatoes. Add water as needed for a thick, saucy gravy. Simmer on low heat for 25–30 minutes, lightly mashing a few beans against the side to thicken naturally.
Finish with garam masala, amchur, and salt. Garnish with fresh coriander.

For tandoori roti: knead whole wheat flour with salt and water into a firm dough. Rest 20 minutes. Divide into 80 g portions, roll into rounds, and cook in a hot tandoor or on a tawa. Brush with ghee before serving.
Serve rajma aloo hot with tandoori roti.
notes: Contains gluten (wheat roti) and dairy (ghee).

sections.heading: For the rajma
items: 3 kg red kidney beans (rajma), soaked overnight

method: Drain soaked rajma and pressure cook in fresh water with salt until completely soft, about 25–30 minutes. Do not drain — the starchy cooking liquid is essential for a thick gravy.
Heat oil in large pots, add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add chopped onions and fry until deep golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes. Add tomato puree, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, and coriander powder. Cook until masala is well-fried and oil separates.

Add the cooked rajma along with all the cooking liquid. Bring to a simmer and cook on low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Mash a few beans against the pot wall to naturally thicken the gravy.
Finish with garam masala and salt. The gravy should be thick and hearty. Garnish with fresh coriander.
For the rice: wash basmati rice and soak 30 minutes. Bring salted water to a boil, add drained rice, and cook until just done. Drain and let steam, covered, for 5 minutes.
Serve rajma ladled generously over steamed basmati rice.

dish_name: Soya Chunk Masala w/ Orange Rice

sections.heading: For the soya chunk masala
items: 3 kg soya chunks (meal maker / textured vegetable protein)

method: Soak soya chunks in boiling hot salted water for 15 minutes until they puff up and soften. Squeeze out all excess water firmly — this step is critical to avoid a spongy texture. Set aside.
Heat oil in large pans, add cumin seeds. Sauté chopped onions until golden brown, about 12 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes. Add tomato puree, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook on high heat until oil separates, about 15 minutes.
Lower heat, add whisked yoghurt gradually, stirring continuously. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add squeezed soya chunks. Toss well to coat in the masala. Add enough water for a semi-thick gravy. Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Finish with crushed kasuri methi, garam masala, and salt. Garnish with coriander.

For orange rice: soak rice 30 minutes. Heat ghee, crackle cumin seeds and bay leaves. Add grated carrots, sauté 3 minutes. Add drained rice, turmeric, and paprika. Stir, then add water and salt. Boil, cover, cook low for 18 minutes.
Fluff rice — it should be a warm orange hue. Serve soya chunk masala alongside.
notes: Contains soy (soya chunks) and dairy (yoghurt, ghee).

sections.heading: Ingredients
items: 3 kg canned San Marzano or Italian plum tomatoes, crushed by hand
Salt and black pepper to taste

method: Bring very large pots of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Cook spaghetti until al dente — about 1 minute less than package instructions. Reserve 2 litres of starchy pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in large wide pans over medium-low heat. Add sliced garlic and chilli flakes. Cook very gently for 2–3 minutes until garlic is golden and fragrant — do not burn.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, sugar, and salt. Increase heat and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and intensifies in flavour.
Tear most basil leaves and fold into the sauce during the last 5 minutes.

Add drained spaghetti directly to the sauce pans. Toss vigorously with tongs over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, adding pasta water a ladle at a time until the sauce emulsifies and clings to each strand.
Season with black pepper. Serve twirled into portions, topped with grated Parmesan and a fresh basil leaf.
notes: Contains gluten (wheat pasta) and dairy (Parmesan cheese).

dish_name: Veg Aloo Khorma w/ Bagara Rice

sections.heading: For the veg aloo khorma
items: 1 kg mixed vegetables (carrots, beans, cauliflower), cut into bite-size pieces
500 g onions, thinly sliced and fried crispy
300 g cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste
40 g poppy seeds (khus khus), soaked and ground to paste

method: Boil potato cubes and mixed vegetables separately until just tender. Drain and reserve.
Heat ghee in large heavy pots. Add whole spices (cumin, bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon) and let them release aroma.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes. Add half the fried onions, kashmiri chilli, and turmeric. Stir well.
Add cashew paste, poppy seed paste, and whisked yoghurt. Cook on low heat, stirring continuously, for 10 minutes.
Add boiled vegetables and potatoes. Pour in coconut milk and enough water for a rich, creamy korma gravy. Simmer for 20 minutes on low heat.
Finish with white pepper, salt, and remaining fried onions on top. Garnish with fresh mint.

For bagara rice: cook basmati rice in salted boiling water until just done. Drain and spread on trays. Heat ghee, add mustard seeds, cumin, dried chillies. Add urad dal and chana dal, fry until golden. Add curry leaves, turmeric, and peanuts. Pour tempering over rice and toss gently.
Serve aloo khorma alongside fragrant bagara rice.
notes: Contains dairy (ghee, yoghurt), tree nuts (cashews), peanuts, and coconut.

sections.heading: For the biryani vegetables
items: 500 g green beans, cut into 2 cm pieces

sections.heading: For the biryani rice
items: 1 g saffron strands, soaked in 200 ml warm milk

sections.heading: For the Dormers' paneer (side)
items: 3 kg paneer, cut into 2 cm cubes

method: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes. Parboil rice in large pots of salted water with whole spices until 70% cooked (the grain should still have a firm bite in the centre). Drain immediately.
Heat oil in large heavy-bottomed pots. Fry sliced onions until deep golden. Remove half for garnish. To the remaining onions, add ginger-garlic paste, cook 3 minutes.
Add all vegetables, biryani masala, chilli powder, turmeric, yoghurt, and salt. Cook on high heat for 10 minutes. Vegetables should be par-cooked, not fully done.
Layer parboiled rice over the vegetable masala. Drizzle saffron milk, scatter mint, coriander, fried onions, and dots of ghee over the rice.
Seal the pot tightly with foil and a heavy lid. Cook on very low heat (dum) for 25–30 minutes. Do not open the lid during this time.

For the paneer side: fry paneer cubes until golden. In separate pans, cook onion puree in ghee until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, and spices. Cook until oil separates. Add cashew paste, yoghurt, water, and simmer. Finish with cream, kasuri methi, garam masala, and sugar. Fold in paneer.
Gently open biryani pot and fold rice and vegetables from bottom up, being careful not to break the grains. Serve biryani with Dormers' paneer on the side.
notes: Contains dairy (paneer, yoghurt, ghee, cream) and tree nuts (cashews). Saffron used.

sections.heading: Ingredients
items: 5 kg basmati or jasmine rice, cooked and cooled (ideally day-old)
500 g spring onions, sliced (white and green separated)
100 ml rice vinegar or white vinegar
200 g spring onion greens for garnish

method: Cook rice a day ahead if possible, or cook fresh rice and spread on large trays to cool completely — this ensures individual grains and prevents clumping.
Heat vegetable oil in very large woks or flat-bottomed pans on highest heat. Add minced garlic and ginger, toss for 30 seconds.
Add white parts of spring onions, carrots, and French beans. Stir-fry on high heat for 3 minutes.
Add cabbage and bell peppers. Stir-fry for 2 more minutes — vegetables should stay crunchy.
Push vegetables to the sides, add the cold rice to the centre. Break up any clumps with a spatula. Toss everything together.
Drizzle soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame oil over the rice. Toss vigorously on high heat for 3–4 minutes until every grain is coated and slightly toasted.
Season with white pepper and salt. Garnish with spring onion greens.
Serve immediately while hot and steaming.
notes: Contains soy (soy sauce) and sesame.

sections.heading: For the soya biryani masala
items: 3 kg soya chunks, soaked in hot water, squeezed dry

sections.heading: For the biryani rice
items: 1 g saffron strands, soaked in 200 ml warm milk

sections.heading: For the raita
items: 500 g cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
100 g tomatoes, deseeded and finely diced

method: Soak soya chunks in boiling water for 15 minutes. Squeeze out all excess water thoroughly. Set aside.
Soak basmati rice 30 minutes. Parboil in large pots of salted water with whole spices until 70% cooked. Drain immediately.
Heat oil in large pots, fry sliced onions until deep golden. Remove half for layering. Add ginger-garlic paste to the pot, cook 3 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, all dry spices, and yoghurt. Cook until masala is well-fried, about 10 minutes. Add squeezed soya chunks and par-boiled potatoes. Toss on high heat for 5 minutes.
Layer parboiled rice over the soya masala. Drizzle saffron milk, scatter mint, coriander, fried onions, and dots of ghee.
Seal the pot with foil and a heavy lid. Cook on very low heat (dum) for 25–30 minutes without opening.
For raita: whisk yoghurt until smooth. Fold in grated cucumber, onions, tomatoes, mint, roasted cumin, chilli powder, and salt. Chill until service.
Gently open biryani and fold from bottom up. Serve soya biryani with a generous side of cold raita.
notes: Contains soy (soya chunks), dairy (yoghurt, ghee). Saffron used.
